inspiration: Damage batching per attack: gather pending damage per target and apply once at the end (weapons.qc lines 202-224). Defect: a new target flushes the previous one, so alternating hits split into separate applications. Fix: keep a small per-target list and flush once per attack. Keep the idea.
Blood as a one-count, visible-only event (weapons.qc lines 151-155). Keep the send-to-visible-clients idea; change the effect to sparks or embers on armour.
Melee as a short forward line test from body height (weapons.qc lines 62-69). Keep the reach test; change the swing to an arc.
Area-damage visibility: a trace to the target centre plus offset points decides whether splash reaches (combat.qc lines 47-72). Keep the multi-point check with our own sample pattern.
Named sound channels: each role has its own channel, so a weapon sound does not cut an item sound (weapons.qc line 449). Keep the channel-per-role idea.
Repeat cues throttled with a timestamp so a looping effect does not spam the mix (combat.qc line 212).
Per-entity precache lists as literal asset-path tables (weapons.qc line 40). Idea: per-zone asset manifests for preloading.

briefs.label: Melee sweep with a short reach test (item)
briefs.why: A short forward test from body height gives a clear hit window; the swing is the readable part at phone width.
briefs.keep: a short reach test from chest height; one hit window per swing; a sound on the weapon channel
briefs.change: an arc sweep instead of a straight line; our own weapon silhouette; a different swing sound

briefs.label: Blood event burst (effect)
briefs.why: One short burst per hit, sent only to clients that can see it, keeps the screen readable in a crowd.
briefs.keep: one event per hit; only visible clients receive it; short life
briefs.change: sparks or embers on armour instead of blood; our own palette; a different burst shape

briefs.label: Splash visibility with offset samples (area effect)
briefs.why: Checking the centre and four offset points makes area hits fair around a corner.
briefs.keep: a multi-point visibility check for area effects; the check is separate from the damage
briefs.change: our own sample pattern and point count; our own splash shape
